summary: The implementation follows the repository's pinning, least-privilege, and executable-policy conventions. The contributor-facing validation documentation has drifted from the workflows and validator scope.

findings.title: Refresh the documented validation and malware workflow contract
findings.problem: The validation description omits the release-token, draft publication, SPDX, and Scorecard policies now enforced by validate_repo.py. It also identifies the advisory malware workflow as v1.0.1 at 7a825d..., while the checked-in workflow uses the newer v1.0.2 pin at 733acb.... Contributors following this section cannot reliably reconcile local checks with the current CI contract.
findings.current_code: The validation script checks skill frontmatter ... dependency-gate workflow structure ... v1.0.1 / 7a825d...
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the current release, SPDX, Scorecard, dependency, and action-pin validations, and update the reusable malware workflow version and full SHA to match the checked-in workflow.
findings.resolution: README now documents the current validation scope and the v1.0.2 reusable malware workflow SHA.

positive_changes: Third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs with version comments.
Repository validation converts permission boundaries, action pins, and workflow separation into executable policy.
The exact workflow-shape assertions fail closed when security-sensitive release steps are changed.
notes: The validator's strict step counts and mapping equality create maintenance friction, but they are an intentional fail-closed policy in this security-sensitive path rather than a correctness defect.
